slides.texte_overlay:
small daily habits of
quietly brilliant people

a walk to think

they take a short walk with no headphones when they're stuck on a problem. moving your body and leaving your mind free is where most good ideas quietly arrive.

writing it out

they write their thoughts down before making a big decision. putting a messy problem on paper makes it smaller and clearer than it ever is when it stays in your head.

a daily lesson

they spend 5 minutes a day learning something new on purpose: a scientific idea, a famous artwork, a moment in history. tiny daily inputs add up to a brilliant mind over time.
slides.texte_sophia:
a daily lesson

i spend 5 minutes a day learning something new on purpose: a scientific idea, an artwork. i do it with the Sophia app, one lesson a day, and tiny daily inputs really add up.

slides.texte_overlay:
reading the original

they read the actual book or study instead of only the summary. going to the source is slower, but it gives you all the nuance that everyone else missed.

early to bed

they protect their sleep like an important appointment. a rested brain learns, remembers and solves problems far better than a tired one, and they know it's not a luxury.
